title: Documentation support (MEAT) for chronic conditions
question: Which chronic condition, if any, is supported for risk adjustment by this note? Ignore the reason for the visit. Choose 'no code' if none is supported.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for persistent joint pain and stiffness.

HPI
The patient is an 80-year-old male presenting for a scheduled follow-up regarding chronic discomfort in his bilateral knees and hips. He reports that the stiffness is most pronounced in the morning and after periods of prolonged sitting. He describes the pain as a dull ache, rated as a 4/10, which occasionally sharpens during heavy exertion like walking long distances. He has been consistent with his current regimen but notes that the stiffness in his left knee has persisted for approximately three weeks. He denies any recent falls, new swelling, redness, or warmth in the joints. He denies any systemic symptoms such as fever, chills, or unexplained weight loss.

Review of Systems
The patient denies chest pain, shortness of breath, or palpitations. He denies recent headaches or dizziness. He reports no changes in bowel or bladder habits. He denies any recent cough or sore throat. He denies any new numbness or tingling in his extremities.

Social History
The patient lives at home with his wife. He is retired and spends most of his time gardening and walking. He denies tobacco use and reports social drinking of one glass of wine on weekends.

Family History
His father had hypertension and a history of stroke. His mother had osteoarthritis.

Medication List
Lisinopril 10mg daily
Atorvastatin 20mg daily
Sertraline 50mg daily
Naproxen 250mg as needed for joint pain

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented x3. He appears in no acute distress. Physical examination reveals bilateral knee joint swelling with mild tenderness to palpation over the patellar tendons. Range of motion is limited by discomfort but is otherwise intact. His gait is steady with a slight limp on the left side. No erythema or warmth is noted.

Vitals
BP: 132/84 mmHg
HR: 72 bpm
Temp: 98.6 F
RR: 16 breaths/min
SpO2: 97% on room air

Recent Labs
HbA1c: 6.8%
eGFR: 65 mL/min/1.73m2
TSH: 2.1 mIU/L

Assessment
The patient is experiencing chronic joint discomfort consistent with his known history. He is managing his symptoms well but requires continued monitoring of inflammation.

Plan
1. Continue current medication list as prescribed.
2. Instructed to use naproxen only as needed for acute flare-ups.
3. Recommend physical therapy twice weekly for strengthening exercises.
4. Follow up in 8 weeks for a reassessment of joint mobility.

Electronically signed, H. Tanaka, MD, 05/14/2026
explanations: An antidepressant on the list does not establish major depression; coders do not infer diagnoses from medications.

distractors.why: Only the provider can document a diagnosis.
